rationale: Retain Cordelio Power as a historical acquired platform, but end CPP Investments' direct ownership when Pattern Energy's share-based acquisition closed on April 1, 2026. Pattern integrated Cordelio's core assets, pipeline and team, while CPP's continuing exposure is represented only on the canonical Pattern Energy record. Correct Cordelio's canonical geography and headquarters, its historical 100% CPP stake, and the acquisition timeline without inferring dissolution of the surviving legal entities.

beforeImage.name: Cordelio Power
beforeImage.description: Cordelio Power develops, builds, and operates wind, solar, and energy-storage projects in the United States and Canada. Its customers are utilities, corporates, and other power offtakers that contract for renewable generation and related capacity. The business is asset-heavy and largely contracted because value is linked to owned and under-construction projects plus a sizable development pipeline. Public company materials have described an operating portfolio of 1,860 MW across the United States and Canada and a U.S. development pipeline of more than 18,000 MW. Pattern Energy completed its acquisition of Cordelio in April 2026 after the platform had been wholly owned by CPP Investments, and the direct ownership percentages of the resulting structure have not been publicly disclosed.
beforeImage.headquarters: New York; Illinois; Oregon; Ontario; British Columbia

milestones.event: CPP Investments completed the acquisition of a 396 MW portfolio of contracted renewable energy projects in Canada through Cordelio Power.
Cordelio Power sold its 6 GW joint venture interest to BrightNight.
Pattern Energy and Cordelio announced a definitive agreement for Pattern to acquire the company.

afterImage.name: Cordelio Power
afterImage.description: Cordelio Power was a Toronto-headquartered wind, solar and energy-storage platform operating in Canada and the United States. CPP Investments wholly owned the business from its June 29, 2018 entry until Pattern Energy's share-based acquisition closed on April 1, 2026. Pattern acquired approximately 1,550 MW across 16 operating or construction projects, most of Cordelio's U.S. development portfolio and the Cordelio team; Cordelio is therefore retained as a historical acquired company subordinate to Pattern, not as a separate active CPP Investments PortCo. CPP's continuing exposure is represented through its 69.1% ownership of Pattern. BrightNight separately announced on April 21, 2026 that it had acquired Cordelio's interest in a 6 GW development joint venture, a partial asset-level divestiture rather than a second company-level exit. Public sources reviewed do not establish the exact surviving merger entity, so dissolution is not inferred.

milestones.event: Cordelio Power was established as CPP Investments' renewable-power platform.
CPP Investments completed its initial 396 MW Canadian renewable-energy acquisition through Cordelio Power.
Pattern Energy's acquisition closed, ending CPP Investments' direct Cordelio ownership and integrating the company into Pattern.
Pattern Energy and Cordelio announced a definitive share-based agreement for Pattern to acquire the company.
